newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Women of banned Malaysian sect renounce teachings.
newsitem.headline: Women of banned Malaysian sect renounce teachings.

text.p: One hundred women who were part of the outlawed Al-Arqam sect formally renounced their former beliefs on Monday, the national news agency Bernama reported.

Murshidah Mustafa, a Moslem religious lawyer, read out a joint declaration at a news briefing in Kuala Lumpur, ending nearly two years of rehabilitation by Pusat Islam, Malaysia's religious advisory council, Bernama said.
The women are workers of Solehah Enterprise, owned by Hatijah Aam, the wife of the movement's former leader, Ashaari Muhammad.
Hatijah is serving a restricted residence order in a suburb of Kuala Lumpur. Murshidah is Ashaari's daughter-in-law.

Murshidah said: "We were so engrossed in developing our own identity without giving any thought that this may not be in line with the government's aspirations. We lived in a world of our own, ignoring the wishes of the government to the extent that we created problems with the government."
The sect was banned by the Malaysian government for teaching a deviant strain of Islam.
